clue.text: This supporter shares our confidence

parts.note: the saying 'between you, me and the ...' marks a secret, so the post that holds up a gate is pictured as party to our confidences

explanation.surface: A loyal backer is let in on our secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' sounds like a loyal friend, but it is a post that holds up a gate, invoked by the phrase 'between you, me and the gatepost', meaning in strict confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate hangs from an upright post, and the idiom 'between you, me and the gatepost' means told in secret.

clue.text: .Gateshead — fish, fish, fish

parts.note: read as 'Gates head': the head, or first letter, of Gates
a ray is a flat fish
a ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A list of fish caught at Gateshead, the town on the Tyne.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split it as 'Gates head' to get G.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Black creature wrongly thought to be a natural at dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters are moving about, so the three words beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark spider was mistakenly believed to make people dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls tarantism, the old belief that a spider's bite caused frenzied dancing (hence the tarantella).
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, often dark-coloured.

clue.text: Letters for Father Bear

explanation.surface: Writing to Daddy Bear, as in the nursery tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Father is PA; its letters, spelt out in words, are 'P and A'. The surface evokes Father Bear from Goldilocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pa is written with a P and an A, and a panda is a black-and-white bear from China.

clue.text: Remove master from Greyfriars after second crushing remark

indicators.note: after places the schoolmaster's name after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: Mr Quelch is the form master of the Remove at Greyfriars, Billy Bunter's school in Frank Richards's stories

explanation.surface: Instructions to sack a schoolmaster after a cutting comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' looks like a verb but is a class: the Remove was a form in British public schools, and Mr Quelch teaches it at Greyfriars in the Billy Bunter stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is a retort that silences or crushes someone.

clue.text: The way sheets of paper burn

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ream is a bundle of 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A remark on how pages catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like a verb about fire, but it is the Scottish word for a small river.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn is the Scottish and northern English word for a brook or small river.

clue.text: He may perform with a flourish

definitions.text: He may perform with a flourish

parts.words: He may perform with a flourish
parts.note: a flourish is also a fanfare of brass, so this musician plays one

explanation.surface: A showman who performs flamboyantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' suggests showy style; a flourish is a fanfare of brass.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player sounding fanfares plays the instrument named in this word.

clue.text: Compound for flavouring essences for the Queen of Persia, say

indicators.note: say signals that the queen's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: in the Bible Esther became queen to the Persian king Ahasuerus

explanation.surface: A chemical used in flavours for a Persian queen's perfumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters are organic chemicals with fruity smells, much used in artificial flavourings.

clue.text: Girl on the verge of crime

parts.note: May is a girl's name
a hem is a border, or verge, of cloth

explanation.surface: A girl about to commit an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the verge of' reads as 'about to'; here 'on' places MAY above HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, mayhem is the crime of maiming someone; generally violent disorder.

clue.text: Damage, that is to say, based on two articles

indicators.note: based on means the first piece stands on top of what follows in this down entry

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is Latin for 'that is to say'
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A remark on harm, explained by two grammatical words.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the abbreviation of scilicet, meaning namely, used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old verb meaning to harm or injure, surviving in 'scathing' and 'unscathed'.

clue.text: Product of Eden's first showing, say

definitions.text: Product of Eden's first showing, say

parts.words: Product of Eden's first showing, say
parts.note: in Genesis Adam and Eve, ashamed of being seen naked, sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves; that garment was made in Eden

explanation.surface: Something that came out of a garden's opening display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' suggests a performance; here it is Adam and Eve's nakedness first being seen. The King James Bible says they sewed fig leaves and 'made themselves aprons'; an apron is also the stage area in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The King James Bible says Adam and Eve sewed fig leaves into this garment to cover themselves.

clue.text: Elevated land away from the coast

parts.note: elevated means raised, or up
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A description of high ground lying inland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland regions far from the sea are said to be upcountry.

clue.text: Student with a university permit for an old car

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car
with can mean and
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A student and a university pass entitle someone to drive a vintage motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A landaulet was an early motor car with a folding hood over the rear seats, named after a carriage style.

clue.text: Resolve sentence into equal quarters

parts.note: par means equal, as in 'on a par'
S and E are two quarters of the compass, south and east

explanation.surface: Instructions to split a sentence into four equal parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests division into four; here it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to analyse or break it down grammatically into its component parts.

clue.text: Nurse is hours in casualty

indicators.note: a casualty is something wrecked or damaged, so the letters of the two words beside it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A nurse spends many hours in the hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casualty' suggests the hospital's accident ward; it signals rearranging HOURS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient or a plant is to feed and sustain it so it thrives.

clue.text: Roman characters would never show stress thus

definitions.text: Roman characters would never show stress thus

parts.words: Roman characters would never show stress thus
parts.note: roman type is upright, so emphasis shown by slanted type is something upright letters could never do

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans never showed their strain this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman characters' suggests people of Rome; it is upright typeface, the opposite of slanted type used for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting words in sloping type is the usual way to emphasise them in print.

clue.text: The whole medical group takes umbrage

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
umbrage is offence or anger, ire

explanation.surface: An entire hospital team takes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete, with nothing missing, is what whole and this adjective both mean.

clue.text: Does it shoot down castles in the air?

definitions.text: Does it shoot down castles in the air?

parts.words: Does it shoot down castles in the air?
parts.note: in chess a castle is also a rook, and rooks are crows that fly, so a gun for shooting those birds would down castles in the air

explanation.surface: A question about a weapon that destroys daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castles in the air' are idle fantasies; chess castles are rooks, also birds, and a small-bore rifle was made for shooting them.
explanation.definitionFit: This light rifle was traditionally used for shooting crows and rabbits.

clue.text: Turn out the guard, my girl!

indicators.note: turn out suggests rearranging, so the letters of the two words beside it are reordered

explanation.surface: A military command to parade the sentries, followed by an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out the guard' is a military order; here 'Turn out' signals an anagram of THE GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's female child is affectionately called 'my girl'.

clue.text: Banger used in inconclusive naval battle

indicators.note: inconclusive means without its conclusion, so the battle's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Salamis was the sea battle of 480 BC where the Greeks beat the Persian fleet

explanation.surface: A firework went off during an indecisive sea fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' looks like a firework or explosion; it is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for a sausage, and salami is a cured spicy sausage.

clue.text: Stay near at hand

explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to abide or exist within, and 'in here' as two words means close by, in this place.

clue.text: Dance music around both sides of Rio

parts.note: CA (circa) means around or about
taken as written
the same abbreviation again: 'both sides of' places it on each side

explanation.surface: Samba-style tunes heard all around Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, the Latin abbreviation for about; Rio de Janeiro's natives are themselves called cariocas, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The carioca is a Brazilian samba-like dance, and the name is also used for its music.

clue.text: Extremely cruel sound of Isabella's brother

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremities, the first and last letters of cruel

parts.note: audio means sound, as in audio equipment

explanation.surface: The harsh voice of a woman's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Measure for Measure, Isabella pleads for her brother's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio is the young man condemned to death in Measure for Measure, whose sister Isabella is a novice nun.

clue.text: It helps to carry a gun, though easily bent

definitions.text: It helps to carry a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A limber is the two-wheeled cart towing a field gun, and limber also means supple or flexible.

clue.text: Is a medical man in eyes, say, or, feet?

indicators.note: in tells us the article and the doctor sit inside the pair of letters

parts.note: eyes sounds like I's, two letter Is
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether a doctor is in your eyes, or your feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is just a link. 'feet' are metrical feet in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical unit of a short syllable then a long one; these are the plural units of verse rhythm.

clue.text: You can see the mark of this dresser on the stone

definitions.text: You can see the mark of this dresser on the stone

parts.words: You can see the mark of this dresser on the stone
parts.note: a dresser here is one who dresses, or shapes, stone, and such craftsmen cut a personal sign into each block

explanation.surface: Someone's piece of furniture has left a stain on the stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresser' suggests furniture or a person dressing; it is someone dressing stone, who carves a personal mason's mark on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason dresses, or shapes, blocks of stone and cuts a personal mark into them.

clue.text: Try some of the mat finish in front of the fireplace

definitions.note: a phrase naming where the thing lies, standing for the thing placed there

indicators.note: finish means the next piece comes at the end of the word

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word 'the' is used, its opening pair

parts.note: a rug is a mat

explanation.surface: Advice to test part of a matt surface by the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes TH from 'the', and 'finish' puts RUG (mat) last. 'mat finish' reads like a non-glossy paint surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is the small carpet laid on the floor just before the grate.

clue.text: The wrong end of the cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: end of tells us to take the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Getting the bad end of a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wrong end' reads as an idiom; split it as TORT (legal wrong) plus the last letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich, often layered, gateau of central European style.

clue.text: Stung into action, champion rider takes a toss

parts.note: the champion is the best

indicators.note: a toss is a fall from a horse, so the letters of rider are thrown about

explanation.surface: A top jockey falls off and is roused to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a toss' pictures a rider thrown; it signals rearranging RIDER into IRRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roused or spurred into moving is to be bestirred.

clue.text: Mounting row about fine — and the repair work

indicators.note: about means the turned row wraps round the abbreviation for fine
mounting means climbing, so the word row is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rising argument over a penalty, plus the cost of mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but is a tier; 'Mounting' turns TIER to REIT, with F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation or overhaul, especially of a ship.

clue.text: Park keeper in a right bait

parts.note: in British slang to be in a bait is to be in a temper, so bait means anger

explanation.surface: A park warden who is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bait' suggests fishing; it is old British schoolboy slang for a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a warden who patrols and looks after a park or forest.

clue.text: Order a beer for one who has gone on ahead

definitions.text: one who has gone on ahead

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so the letters of the three words beside it are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pub request on behalf of a friend who went in first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a bar request; it signals rearranging A BEER FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor has gone before us in time, hence a forebear; a euphemistic description of a forefather.
